subject.title: [Feature]: Support for sandbox Docker parameters (--gpus all, --ipc=host)

question: Should OpenClaw add a narrow host IPC Docker sandbox option, reject host IPC, or design a broader dangerous Docker namespace policy first?
rationale: Host IPC changes the sandbox isolation boundary, and current sandbox config intentionally uses typed, validated fields rather than arbitrary Docker argument passthrough.

options.title: Add Narrow Host IPC Field
options.body: Add a typed, explicitly dangerous host IPC option with schema, create-args, docs, config-hash, and security-audit coverage while keeping raw passthrough unsupported.

options.title: Reject Host IPC
options.body: Keep Docker sandbox isolation tighter and close the host IPC portion as unsupported, leaving GPU passthrough as the supported high-power path.

options.title: Design Broader Namespace Policy
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers define one policy for IPC, PID, network namespace joins, and related dangerous Docker options.

recommendation.title: Add Narrow Host IPC Field
recommendation.body: Add a typed, explicitly dangerous host IPC option with schema, create-args, docs, config-hash, and security-audit coverage while keeping raw passthrough unsupported.

likelyOwner.reason: This team owns the sandbox and security-sensitive paths that would need to approve a namespace-isolation tradeoff.
